method: Source-confirmed binding defects in public BUIDL CTC submissions, each read in the re-cloned repository and, where possible, corroborated by a live keyless probe or the ThirdCheck analyzer. Public artifact: the anti-pattern is described without the author. The named basis is held privately for coordinated disclosure and is available to the sponsor on request.

confirmed.summary: Every registration path verifies through a verifier interface's verifySingle / verifyBatch at 0x0FD2, selectors the precompile does not implement, and the verifier is an unguarded swappable address with a mock shipped in the production source tree.
evidence: Lending.sol:160 calls IVerifier(target).verifySingle on every registration path
MockPrecompile.sol:10 mock returning true shipped in the production src tree
the absence-proof generator blanks the proof on failure but returns success:true (generateAbsenceProof.ts:125)
confirmed.liveProof: npm run judge:verify shows 0x0FD2 replies 'Unknown selector' to verifySingle while dispatching verify
confirmed.reproduce: npm run judge:verify -- --reclone (requires the private reclone module)

confirmed.class: protocol proof replaced by a centralized signature
confirmed.summary: Presents itself as an Attestcoin consumer but verifies its 'attestation' with an off-chain ECDSA signature (ecrecover) against an owner-set validator, and never calls the precompile anywhere in the repo. Credit limits are set on that signature; a compromised or malicious validator key mints arbitrary credit.
evidence: no verify / verifyAndEmit / calculateTxIndex / 0x0FD2 reference anywhere in the repository
confirmed.liveProof: n/a (source fact); the ThirdCheck analyzer flags it as 'Attestation verified by signature, not the precompile'
confirmed.reproduce: scan with the analyzer: analyzeTree over the cloned repo yields the B-11 signature-not-precompile finding

confirmed.class: on-chain recorder discards the proof and trusts unauthenticated caller data
confirmed.summary: The on-chain 'verify' function takes a proof and discards it (a bare no-op), performs no precompile call, and records a payment event, mints a credit passport, and writes to the registry entirely from caller-supplied values. It has no access control, so anyone can fabricate an invoice payment and mint themselves a credit passport for free. The project's own README states the on-chain verifyAndEmit selector did not match on this testnet, so verification was moved off-chain, leaving the on-chain record unauthenticated. This independently corroborates the selector finding of consumer-A and adds a distinct class: verification claimed off-chain, on-chain record forgeable.
evidence: Verifier.sol:62 verifyAndRecord is external with no access-control modifier
Verifier.sol:76 the proof parameter is discarded, never decoded or verified
Verifier.sol:89 emits a payment event from caller-supplied payer/beneficiary/amount
no verifyAndEmit / calculateTxIndex / EvmV1Decoder / 0x0FD2 reference anywhere in the contract
confirmed.liveProof: n/a (source fact); the ThirdCheck analyzer flags it as 'Records an attestation without verifying the proof'
confirmed.reproduce: analyzeTree over the cloned repo yields the B-11 discarded-proof finding
